title: The Toy Boat
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 1, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds ea, oy, ir
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'oy' — another way to write the /oi/ sound your child knows from 'coin', used at the end of words like toy, boy and joy.

pages.illustration: Ned the duckling holding up a small wooden toy boat with both flippers, presenting it to the reader with enormous pride.
Close on the boat itself: pillar-box red hull, white sail, chipped paint showing it is well loved. Beautiful object detail.

pages.text: Ned put it in the pond.
pages.illustration: Ned crouched at the pond edge lowering the boat onto the water, tongue out with concentration, ripples spreading from it.
The boat sailing out across the open water, small and upright, its reflection beneath it. Wide calm pond, lots of water.
Moss arriving at the bank with his own toy — a squat wooden tug — held awkwardly in both paws. Slightly embarrassed, very endearing.

pages.text: The toys ran into a rock.
pages.illustration: The two toys colliding beside a grey rock, one tipping, a small collision splash. Both owners' faces caught mid-horror on the bank.
Ned with both wings on his head and beak wide open in dismay, close-cropped so the alarm fills the page.

pages.text: It was fun. The toys were good.
pages.illustration: Both boats bobbing upright again, entirely undamaged, one still gently spinning. Relief on the bank behind them.
Ned airborne with joy, both wings up, boat clutched to his chest. Water droplets flying. Pure celebration.
Closing page: the two of them on the bank at golden hour with both boats out drying on the grass, sitting close together. Warm and content.
